name: Why does interior wear and tear appear more frequently in Denver area homes?

mainEntity.name: Why does interior wear and tear appear more frequently in Denver area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, seasonal humidity drops and temperature shifts between dry winters and wet springs cause wooden framing and drywall joints to expand and contract frequently. This climate cycle often creates recurring hairline cracks at drywall ceiling seams, separation along baseboard caulking, and sticking interior doors in communities from Aurora to Centennial and Parker. Repairs in this region require flexible caulking and proper drywall taping techniques that tolerate local climate movement without splitting open during dry months.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's dry winters and temperature swings cause wood framing to expand and shrink, leading to cracked drywall joints, split baseboard caulk, and sticking doors.
